newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Olympic Committee to aid NCAA sports programs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Olympic Committee to aid NCAA sports programs.

text.p: The U.S. Olympic Committee (USOC) Saturday voted to strengthen its ties to American colleges and universities with an $8 million grant programme aimed at increasing support for Olympic sports.

On the first of day of its semi-annual meeting, the USOC Board of Directors also elevated the status of national organisations representing water ski and squash, reflecting the inclusion of the sports in the 1999 Pan American Games, a committee spokeswoman said.

The grant programme adopted by the board will award $2 million a year from 1997 through 2000 to conferences in the National Collegiate Athletic Association, for distribution to programmes in conference schools.
Its aim is to "provide incentives for colleges and universities to elevate or enhance their sports programmes," USOC spokeswoman Gayle Bodin said.
The programme also seeks to encourage equitable support for womens' sports and ultimately strengthen U.S. Olympic teams, she said.

All sports included in the Olympic and Pan American games will be eligible for the grants, but aid will be targeted toward emerging womens' sports and sports that have experienced declines in sponsorship.
Targeted sports are: archery, badminton, rowing, gymnastics, ice hockey, swimming, skiing, synchronized swimming, team handball, water polo, wrestling and track and field.
The elevation of U.S. squash and water skiing associations from affiliated to Pan American status, and their recognition as national governing bodies, makes them eligible for USOC grants, Bodin said.
The two sports will be included in the 1999 Pan American Games to be held in the Canadian city of Winnipeg.
Bodin said USOC began the four-year Olympic cycle after last year's Olympics with a $50 million surplus.
The USOC was to conclude its two-day meeting Sunday.
